sections.content: A flat is made of rooms: *a nappali* (living room), *a hálószoba* (bedroom), *a konyha* (kitchen), *a fürdőszoba* (bathroom) and *az előszoba* (hallway). To say what is in a room, put *-ban* or *-ben* on the room and use *van*: *A konyhában van egy asztal.* The room comes first, then *van*, then the thing. *Nincs* says there is none: *A fürdőszobában nincs ablak.*

sections.title: Spelling
sections.content: A final *-a* grows long before the ending: *konyha* becomes *konyhában*, with *á*. *Nappali* ends in *i* and keeps it. The last vowel other than *i* decides between *-ban* and *-ben* (*nappaliban*): *fürdőszoba* begins with front vowels, but it ends in *a*, so it takes *-ban*.

items.english: There is a table in the kitchen.
There is a lamp in the living room.
There is no window in the bathroom.

sections.content: English says “in the” with two small words. Hungarian puts the ending on the room: *a konyhában*. Keep the accent: *konyhaban*, with a short *a*, is a misspelling. Use *az* before a vowel: *az előszobában*.
